query: Why do handling times differ by channel and priority?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: The type of issue plausibly drives both which channel/priority a ticket is routed through (treatment) and how long it takes to handle (outcome), making it a genuine common cause surfaced from the issue_description text.

per_column.name: operational_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity plausibly influences the assigned priority/channel and independently affects handling time, so it is a common cause not stated in the query.

per_column.name: customer_impact_type
per_column.rationale: Impact type can shape prioritization/channel choice and also the effort needed, plausibly a common cause; not named in the query.

per_column.name: scope_blast_radius
per_column.rationale: Blast radius affects both priority assignment and handling effort, a plausible common cause surfaced from text.

per_column.name: root_cause_domain
per_column.rationale: The technical domain of the root cause can influence which channel/team handles it and the time required; arguably a common cause though it borders on being determined post-triage.

per_column.name: requires_engineering_escalation
per_column.rationale: Escalation is more plausibly a consequence of priority/channel on the causal path to longer handling time rather than a common cause; adjusting for it would block part of the effect.

per_column.name: technical_complexity
per_column.rationale: Complexity plausibly drives both priority/channel routing and handling time independently, a genuine common cause not named in the query.

per_column.name: workaround_available
per_column.rationale: Availability of a workaround can influence assigned priority and the handling effort/time, a plausible common cause; some risk it is downstream of triage.

judge.rationale: The treatments (channel and priority) come from the original table, and the added columns are dominated by variables that plausibly cause BOTH the treatment (routing/prioritization) and the outcome (handling time): issue category, operational severity, customer impact, blast radius, and technical complexity are strong common causes surfaced from the issue_description text rather than copied from the query, which only names 'channel' and 'priority'. This demonstrates real causal reasoning. One added column (requires_engineering_escalation) is better read as a mediator on the treatment→outcome path, and a couple (root_cause_domain, workaround_available) sit closer to triage outputs, slightly lowering quality; but the majority are genuine, non-query-named confounders.
